extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users learning TikZ (beginners / students in a LaTeX course)
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step tutorial for creating figures in LaTeX using the PGF/TikZ toolset, covering package loading, coordinate systems, drawing commands, nodes, plotting, loops, and recursive examples (Sierpiński triangle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Load the TikZ package in the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a figure in Ti k Z you will first need to load the correct package in your TeX file, i.e. use \usepackage{tikz} in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a wide range of options and special Ti k Z libraries which can also be used and would need to be loaded specifically (e.g. \usetikzlibrary{math}), but the beginner course omits these. See CTAN, Wikibooks, and TeXample for available libraries and further documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place TikZ figures inside a figure environment for captions/numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: A Ti k Z figure is usually placed in a \begin{figure} LaTeX environment, as you would do with other figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the figure environment allows you to give the figure a number and caption so it can be referenced easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the tikzpicture environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Start a Ti k Z figure by writing the code \begin{tikzpicture} ... \end{tikzpicture} inside (for example) a figure environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may pass options to the tikzpicture environment (e.g. [scale=3]) to scale the whole figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminate every TikZ statement with a semicolon
rubrics_metrics.description: Every line of Ti k Z code must be closed with a semicolon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is syntactic: forgetting semicolons will break the picture compilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate systems: Cartesian and polar; default units
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinates can be given as Cartesian (x,y) using round brackets, e.g. (-2,0) or (1.5,1.5), or in polar form (angle:length) separated by a colon, e.g. (180:2) or (45:2.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no unit is given the default is centimeters; you can mix units like (1cm,2pt). Hint: polar coordinates are useful for placing nodes in a circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw straight lines with \draw and path operators (--, -|, |-)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the \draw command and path operators: -- for a direct straight line, -| or |- to route horizontal then vertical (or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw (-1,0) -- (3,10pt) -- (35:3); produces connected straight segments. Use -| or |- to force an L-shaped path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add drawing options in square brackets (colors, arrows, thickness, patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: The style of the lines can be changed by giving options to the \draw command in square brackets directly after the command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \draw[->] ... draws an arrow; \draw[red] ... changes color; \draw[dotted,gray] ... gives a dotted gray line. Arrow types shown include ->, <->, ->>, <-. Thickness keywords like very thick and patterns like dotted are supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curved lines: 'to' with out/in angles and Bézier curves
rubrics_metrics.description: Curved lines can be drawn with the to operator (allowing out=.. and in=.. angles) or with Bézier syntax using '.. controls (..)..' with one or two control points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: \draw (-1,0) to[out=90,in=135] (5,1); and \draw (-1,0) .. controls (0,-2) and (4,2) .. (5,1); The to form lets you add options to the connecting command; Bézier curves are specified by control points that pull the curve toward them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful: node placement differs when using 'to' vs '--'
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the command to rather than --, the location/syntax of the node command changes slightly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With -- you can write (0,0) -- (1,1) node{...} ; whereas with to you put the node between the coordinates: (0,0) to node{...} (1,1) ; The page shows equivalent code producing the same visual result but different token placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use nodes for labels, text, math and shapes
rubrics_metrics.description: A node is used to write text (or math) at coordinates; nodes can also be surrounded by shapes (circle, rectangle, rounded corners) or be empty shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nodes can be placed inline while drawing or defined separately. Node options include position specifiers (midway, pos=0.75, above, right) and style specifiers (circle,draw), e.g. (0,0) node[circle,draw]{hello}. Nodes can contain math using $...$.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefine and name nodes for prettier connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefine nodes and give them a label so you can draw lines from node to node rather than raw coordinates, which avoids lines starting/ending exactly at defined coordinates and looks better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \node[circle,draw] (label1) at (0,0) { ... }; \node[rectangle,draw] (label2) at (1,1) { ... }; \draw (label1) -- (label2);

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale entire figure using tikzpicture options
rubrics_metrics.description: The option [scale=3] (or other values) at the beginning of the tikzpicture increases the scale of the figure by that factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the option like \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=3] to magnify or shrink the whole picture instead of scaling each element individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot mathematical functions with plot and domain/samples options
rubrics_metrics.description: Ti k Z has a built-in way to plot curves: use \draw [domain=min:max] plot (\x,{<expression>});
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \draw[blue, thick][domain=-2:2, samples=150] plot (\x,{cos(pi*\x r)}) node[right]{$y=\cos(x)$}; Use samples to control plotting resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trig function unit handling: use 'r' to indicate radians
rubrics_metrics.description: When using trig functions in TikZ expressions, append r to the argument to indicate radians (the r in the argument signifies that we enter \x in radians).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: cos(pi*\x r) uses \x in radians; otherwise TikZ's trigonometric functions expect degrees by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw axes and label points manually with \draw and nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: You can add axes and labels to plots by drawing arrowed lines and placing node labels, and draw small filled circles for points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example code draws gray arrowed axes, labels x and y using nodes, and highlights the origin with \draw[fill,gray] (0,0) circle [radius=1pt];

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \foreach loops for repetitive/iterative drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: In Ti k Z it is possible to make use of for loops using \foreach ... in ..., which lets you create repetitive structures quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: \foreach \x in {0,1,2,3} \draw[red,thick] (0,\x) circle [radius=\x+1]; Useful for iterative figures and patterns (Sierpiński triangle uses recursion but loops are useful for iteration).

rubrics_metrics.name: For recursive mathematical drawings use tikzmath and math library
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursive iterative figures (like Sierpiński’s triangle) require a special Ti k Z library (\usetikzlibrary{math}) and \tikzmath to define recursive functions inside the picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page provides a full example: define a helper macro \Triangle to draw a filled equilateral triangle, then define a tikzmath function sierpinski( x,y,s,d ) that recurses to draw smaller triangles and a loop to place multiple iterations side by side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a minimal standalone document skeleton for single-figure PDFs
rubrics_metrics.description: For single-figure PDFs you can use documentclass[border=1cm]{standalone} with \usepackage{tikz} and then a \begin{document} ... \end{document} wrapping the tikzpicture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tutorial supplies a copy-pasteable skeleton so students can focus on TikZ code without other document structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to external resources for more examples and advanced options
rubrics_metrics.description: Three useful references/sources of inspiration are given: the Wikibooks entry on TikZ, the CTAN package page with the official handbook, and the TeXample TikZ database full of examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links: https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/LaTeX/PGF/TikZ , https://www.ctan.org/pkg/pgf , https://texample.net/tikz/ . Use these for learning libraries, styles, and more complex examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints for exercises: use polar coordinates for circular node placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Hint: It might help to define the nodes in a circle using polar coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a practical tip for the exercise to lay out multiple nodes evenly around a circle; polar syntax (angle:radius) is recommended.
